title: Jurisdictional Handshake and Audit Bundle Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational reference for implementing a jurisdiction-aware request handshake and producing an audit-ready evidence bundle for cross-border requests. This is intentionally lightweight and action-focused — the goal is an engineer or oncall to run through an incident and produce defensible artifacts for legal/infosec review.

Scope:
- Applies to Private and Dedicated deployments where a customer has explicit region constraints or contractual territory clauses.
- Covers request routing metadata, ephemeral anchoring (where a request must touch a local anchor), operator evidence packaging, and the minimal telemetry to demonstrate compliance.
- Does NOT replace legal review. This doc maps engineering signals to likely legal needs.

High-level design principles:
- Minimal surface: prefer a few strong signals rather than many weak ones.
- Immutable evidence: when possible, write proof artifacts to an append-only store with monotonic IDs for auditability.
- Separation of concerns: routing decisions vs. evidence collection vs. retention lifecycle.
- Safe defaults: if jurisdiction is ambiguous, prefer local retention and escalate to SRE/Legal.

Core handshake flow (engineer checklist):
1) Ingress parsing: verify incoming region_hint header (x-rdw-region-hint) and customer-declared_jurisdiction in metadata. Accept possible values: region-code (e.g., eu-west-1), country-code (e.g., DE), or explicit policy-id.
2) Local eligibility check: consult regional-capability-cache (in-memory TTL 30s). If match -> mark route:LOCAL.
3) Anchor attempt: if route:LOCAL required by policy, attempt ephemeral-anchor call to local evidence agent (anchor endpoint). If anchor unreachable: fallback to route:REMOTE with recorded fallback_reason.
4) Token tagging: add audit-token to request context (format: rdw-audit-YYYYMMDD-<shortid>). Store mapping in audit-index.
5) Response tagging: attach x-rdw-evidence-id header to downstream response when evidence bundle created.

Evidence bundle spec (minimal set to be audit-ready):
- manifest.json (fields: evidence_id, received_at_ts, ingress_headers, region_decision, route_taken, fallback_reason (if any), operator_id (if manual), policy_version, retention_tier)
- request_proto.bin (raw serialized request body or minimal extract of PII)
- routing_log.txt (line-separated events with timestamps)
- local_anchor_resp.json (if local anchor called, include receipt/signature)
- system_checksums.txt (sha256 for all artifacts)
- chain_of_custody.csv (timestamps, actor, action)
Storage: append-only S3 path (or equivalent local-volume with WORM flag) under customer_audit/<customer_id>/<evidence_id>/
Retention: choose tier based on contract: standard (90 days), extended (365 days), legal-hold (indefinite) — map to customer-contract metadata.

Operator incident runbook (short):
- If customer calls with a cross-border compliance question: gather customer-id, example_request_id, time-window.
- Trigger evidence generation: POST /internal/evidence/generate?req=<request_id> (creates bundle even if not generated live).
- Verify manifest and checksums. Attach evidence-id to ticket and notify Legal via #legal-ask with evidence-id and brief summary.
- If missing local anchor data: record in manifest fallback_reason=anchor-timeout and collect network traces.

Telemetry & signals to emit (minimum):
- rdw.region_decision (LOCAL|REMOTE|AMBIGUOUS)
- rdw.audit_token (short id)
- rdw.evidence_created (bool) + rdw.evidence_id
- rdw.fallback_reason (enum: ANCHOR_TIMEOUT, NO_CAPACITY, POLICY_MISMATCH, MANUAL_OVERRIDE)
- rdw.policy_version (semver)
These should be indexed and queryable for at least 180 days for troubleshooting and 365 days for investigations.

Testing & QA checklist:
- Unit tests for header parsing and policy lookup (happy / malformed / absent headers).
- Integration test that simulates anchor success and anchor failure paths (assert evidence bundle contents).
- Chaos test: kill local_anchor service during a 2h window and verify fallback_reason is set and bundles still generated.
- Mock audit drill: weekly create evidence bundles for a random sample (1/1000 requests) and run manifest validation.

Edge cases & decisions to surface to Legal/Security:
- Partial data retention when only derivable metadata required vs. full request body storage. (Question: do we store request body for all EU requests by default?)
- Handling of cached responses that originated in a different jurisdiction. Document chain_of_custody for cache hits.
- When operator manually overrides (e.g., to expedite a request), record explicit signed operator_id and reason.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Sanity-check retention tiers vs. customer contract templates (owner: Priya).
- Q2: Add cryptographic signing for local_anchor_resp.json? (owner: Lin)
- Q3: Should evidence bundles be hashed and anchored on a public ledger for third-party verifiability? (owner: Marco)
- TODO: Draft short customer-facing FAQ on what we store and how long (owner: Aisha).

References / quick links:
- compliance template: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RegionalContractClauses (internal)
- current policy list: github.com/redwood-inference/policy-configs/tree/main/jurisdictions
- related tickets: JIRA RD-9821 (handshake spec), RD-9950 (evidence-store WORM)

Appendix (example manifest snippet):
{
  "evidence_id": "rdw-e-20260109-7f4b",
  "received_at": "2026-01-09T17:24:12Z",
  "ingress_headers": ["x-rdw-region-hint: eu-west-1", "x-customer-jurisdiction: DE"],
  "region_decision": "LOCAL",
  "route_taken": "LOCAL_ANCHOR_OK",
  "fallback_reason": "",
  "policy_version": "2025.11.4",
  "retention_tier": "extended"
}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a pragmatic, deployable checklist rather than a perfectionist design doc. Looking for: gaps in evidence fields, operational friction, and legal/contract mismatches.
- Prefer short PRs that add manifest fields incrementally instead of a large schema migration.
